questions.question: Think of the hour from 3 o'clock to 4 o'clock on an analog clock as one whole. It is cut into 4 equal parts, and each part is 15 minutes long. Since 3 o'clock, the minute hand has swept through exactly 1 of those 4 equal parts. What time is it?
options: Quarter past 3, which a digital clock shows as 3:15
Quarter to 3, which a digital clock shows as 2:45
Half past 3, which a digital clock shows as 3:30
Quarter past 4, which a digital clock shows as 4:15
questions.explain: One of the 4 equal parts of an hour is one quarter, and 1 quarter of 60 minutes is 15 minutes, so 15 minutes after 3 is quarter past 3 (3:15). The trap is saying quarter to 3, which means 15 minutes BEFORE 3 o'clock.

questions.question: Think of the hour from 7 o'clock to 8 o'clock as one whole. It is cut into 2 equal parts, and each part is 30 minutes long. Since 7 o'clock, the minute hand has swept through exactly 1 of those 2 equal parts, so it is half past 7. What would a digital clock show?
questions.explain: Half of the 60 minutes in an hour is 30 minutes, so half past 7 is 7:30. A common trap is writing 6:30, as if half past meant half an hour before the hour instead of after it.

questions.question: Think of the hour from 9 o'clock to 10 o'clock as one whole, cut into 4 equal parts of 15 minutes each. Since 9 o'clock, 3 of those 4 equal parts have gone by, so a digital clock reads 9:45. What is the usual name for this time?
questions.explain: When 3 of the 4 parts are used up, only 1 quarter (15 minutes) is left until the next hour, so 9:45 is quarter to 10. The trap is keeping the number 9 and saying quarter to 9, but quarter to always names the hour that is coming next.

questions.question: Think of the hour from 2 o'clock to 3 o'clock as one whole, cut into 4 equal parts of 15 minutes each. Since 2 o'clock, 2 of those 4 equal parts have gone by. Which sentence correctly gives the fraction of the hour that has passed and the name of the time?
options: 1/4 of the hour has passed, so it is quarter past 2
2/4 of the hour has passed, so it is quarter past 2
3/4 of the hour has passed, so it is quarter to 3
2/4 of the hour has passed, so it is half past 2
questions.explain: The denominator 4 tells how many equal parts the hour is cut into and the numerator 2 tells how many have passed, and 2/4 is the same as one half, so it is half past 2 (2:30). The trap is seeing the word quarter in 2/4 and calling it quarter past.

questions.question: The digital clock in the kitchen reads 4:45. Which is another way to say this same time?
questions.explain: From 4:45 there are 15 minutes, one quarter of an hour, left before 5 o'clock, so it is quarter to 5. The trap is keeping the 4 you can see on the clock and saying quarter to 4, which would really be 3:45.

questions.question: The BC Ferries departure board uses a 24-hour clock and shows 16:15 for the next sailing. How would you say that time in words on a 12-hour clock?
questions.explain: Subtract 12 from 16 to get 4 in the afternoon, and 15 minutes is one quarter of an hour past that hour, so 16:15 is quarter past 4 in the afternoon. The trap is reading only the 6 in 16 and saying 6 in the evening.

questions.question: Draw a number line in your head from 5:00 to 6:00. It is divided into 4 equal jumps, and each jump is 15 minutes long. A dot sits on the third mark after 5:00. What time is the dot showing?
questions.explain: Three jumps of 15 minutes is 45 minutes past 5, which leaves one quarter of the hour before 6, so the dot is at quarter to 6 (5:45). The trap is counting the marks as quarters that are left instead of quarters that have passed.

questions.question: Sofia's hockey practice at the Burnaby arena starts at half past 6 in the evening. Her mum writes the start time on the fridge calendar using the 24-hour clock. What should she write?
questions.explain: Half past 6 means 30 minutes after 6, and for evening times you add 12 to the hour, so 6:30 in the evening is 18:30. The trap is writing 06:30, which on a 24-hour clock means half past 6 in the morning.

questions.question: Maya's soccer game starts at quarter to 8 in the morning. She tells her dad this means 8:15, because a quarter is 15 minutes. Which statement gives the correct start time and the correct reason?
options: 7:45, because quarter to 8 means one quarter of an hour, 15 minutes, before 8 o'clock
8:45, because three quarters of the hour have gone by after 8 o'clock
8:15, because a quarter of an hour is 15 minutes and you count 15 minutes on from 8 o'clock
7:15, because you take a quarter of an hour away from 7 o'clock
questions.explain: The word to means before, so quarter to 8 is 15 minutes earlier than 8 o'clock, which is 7:45. Maya's mistake is the most common one: using the 15 minutes correctly but counting forward from the hour instead of backward to it.

questions.question: Ella's skating session at the community centre ends at quarter to 5 in the afternoon, and the session lasted 30 minutes. What time did the session start?
questions.explain: First change quarter to 5 into 4:45, then count back 30 minutes to get 4:15, which is quarter past 4. The trap is counting the 30 minutes forward instead of backward, which lands on quarter past 5.

questions.question: Noah wants his alarm to ring at half past 6 in the morning. He types 6:50 into the digital clock, because he thinks half of an hour must be 50. Which time is correct, and why?
options: 6:50, because half of an hour is half of 100, which is 50
6:15, because half of a quarter hour is 15 minutes
6:30, because half of the 60 minutes in an hour is 30 minutes
6:45, because half of the clock face is 45 minutes
questions.explain: An hour has 60 minutes, and one half of 60 is 30, so half past 6 is 6:30. Noah's mistake is treating an hour like 100 units the way we do with dollars and cents; clocks count in 60s, not 100s.

questions.question: Liam's swimming lesson at the pool starts at quarter to 5 in the afternoon and lasts 45 minutes. His swim card must show the finishing time in words and on the 24-hour clock. Which line is correct?
questions.explain: Quarter to 5 is 4:45, and 45 minutes later is 5:30, which is half past 5; because it is the afternoon, add 12 to the hour to get 17:30. The trap is getting 5:30 right but writing it as 05:30, which on a 24-hour clock means half past 5 in the morning.
